newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline propelled higher by futures gains.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline propelled higher by futures gains.

text.p: NWE gasoline was propelled higher by strong gains in related crude and gasoline futures on Monday, traders said.
Eurograde barges traded as high as $202.50 fob ARA in afternoon trade, up from $197.50 done in the morning.
"The $197.50 barge had to be loaded by May 20 which may account for the fairly low price," said one trader.
Players attributed the rise to strong gains in related crude futures and the NYMEX unleaded contract.
June IPE Brent was 66 cents higher at $19.59 a barrel and NYMEX crude some 83 cents up at $21.26 at 1721 GMT.
June NYMEX unleaded futures, meanwhile, were some 1.41 cents higher at 64.30 a gallon-- leaving the all-important arbitrage door wide open.

Despite the opening of the arbitrage door no transatlantic deals were reported, although some six players -- with roughly 120,000 tonnes of suitable gasoline between them -- were reported to be poised to push material westward.
"I haven't seen anything go so far this week but I would expect to see material moving over the next couple of days if the arb stays open," said one trader.
One trader said the arbitrage door only really worked for those with prompt barrels.
"If you've got prompt barrels it works," he said. "You've got to load before May 20, otherwise the backwardation on the gasoline contract makes it more of a gamble."
